# Bounded Native NMPC and Frozen Torque Replay (Provisional)

## Control and Evidence Boundary

F05a (#11904, parent #11789) evaluates an optional robust nonlinear model
predictive controller against the F02 TVLQR controller. The current executable
boundary is a native MuJoCo one-hinge, direct unit-motor, contact-free fixture.
The controller sees exact simulated state at each native 10 ms step; this is not
a camera/marker estimator or a delayed-feedback experiment. A nominal 0.30 kg
prediction model and a 0.42 kg perturbation scenario are declared before the
two initial-angle trials (0.4 and 0.7 rad). The 0.42 kg model is also the
execution plant. The nominal trajectory is the zero angle and zero velocity.

For state $x=(q,v)$, applied motor torque $u$, scenario models $f_s$, horizon
$H=4$, and reference $r$, each attempted plan solves the finite robust problem

$$
\min_{u_{0:H-1}}\;\max_s\left[\sum_{k=1}^{H}
  \|f_s^{(k)}(x,u)-r_k\|_Q^2 + \|u_{k-1}\|_R^2
  + \|f_s^{(H)}(x,u)-r_H\|_{Q_f}^2\right],
$$

subject to per-scenario state bounds, actuator bounds and optional input-slew
bounds. The current solver is SciPy SLSQP shooting with finite-difference
derivatives, a 500-evaluation limit and a cooperative 1 s wall budget. It may
overrun the native step; neither the budget nor a successful solve is a hard
real-time guarantee. Candidate first inputs are admitted only after independent
bound checks and a strict objective improvement over the predeclared verified
fallback. Timeout, cancellation, stale observations, solver failure,
infeasibility and no benefit preserve a labeled fallback command; an unsafe
fallback raises rather than entering the plant. Warm plans shift only after an
accepted solve. Input receipts retain status, evaluation count, elapsed time,
scenario count and the actual post-limit actuator command.

The native adapter preflights the complete `mjSTATE_INTEGRATION` initial state,
model, actuator, time grid and Tools T01 policy with F06. The controlled plant
steps exactly once per command. Afterward the adapter exports the executed ZOH
motor torques and independently replays them in a fresh native instance with a
time-only input player. Position, velocity and full native integration state
must match the controlled trajectory within $10^{-12}$ absolute tolerance.
The same independent replay is required for F02 TVLQR in both paired trials.
No observed state or optimizer callback reaches the frozen replay.

## Paired Trial and Selection

The source-controlled receipt
`docs/development/feedback_controls/F05_NATIVE_PAIRED_RECEIPT_MJ38.json`
binds the supported MuJoCo version, source hashes, exact Tools pin, model,
initial-state, policy and input digests. It records both predeclared trials,
including failed and fallback solves, native replay, angle RMSE, applied effort,
controller-call p50/p95/worst wall times and evaluation counts. The separate
`F05_NATIVE_PAIRED_RECEIPT.json` records an earlier unsupported 3.3.4
development run. Hardware and process load can move latency and even the number
of plans that meet the cooperative budget. Results are not cherry-picked for a
solver-win claim. The accepted engineering disposition is to retain F02 TVLQR
for native-step execution and reject this SciPy shooting prototype as the
real-time/full-swing provider. Its useful result is a fail-closed optimizer,
fallback and independent replay boundary for future derivative-based solvers.

On the supported Windows Python 3.12.10 / MuJoCo 3.8.0 run, the 0.4 rad trial
timed out on all 8 optimizer calls: NMPC angle RMSE was 0.400 versus TVLQR
0.348 rad. At 0.7 rad, only 2 of 8 plans optimized: RMSE was 0.617 versus
0.622 rad. NMPC median controller-call time was about 1.002 s in each trial,
over 100 times the 10 ms native step. A second complete supported-provider
run retained the same 0/8 and 2/8 optimized counts and RMSE values, with
median call times about 1.001 and 1.002 s. The earlier unsupported 3.3.4
development environment produced different accepted-plan counts; this
underscores why provider and load identity belong in the receipt. The small
0.7 rad tracking gain does not offset the native-step latency and the adverse
0.4 rad result.

Reproduce the paired receipt with a supported MuJoCo Python environment:

```powershell
$env:F05_BENCHMARK_RECEIPT='1'
python -m pytest -q -n 0 -o junit_family=legacy tests/unit/motion_matching/test_bounded_nmpc_native.py --junitxml native-paired.xml
python scripts/f05_native_paired_receipt.py --junit native-paired.xml --host-alias local-host --output docs/development/feedback_controls/F05_NATIVE_PAIRED_RECEIPT_MJ38.json
```

The receipt is a one-hinge software benchmark, not evidence of contact/grip
reactions, muscles, manifold dynamics, participant generalization, private
capture accuracy, six-engine parity or full-swing replay. Those gates remain
open under F05/F09/F10; the design-manual calculation registry stays blocked.
